verses.zh: 「你要用皂荚木做一座烧香的坛。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “You are to make an altar for burning incense;[NOTE:2] you are to make it of[NOTE:3] acacia wood.[NOTE:4]
notes: Why this section has been held until now is a mystery. One would have expected to find it with the instructions for the other furnishings. The widespread contemporary view that it was composed later does not answer the question, it merely moves the issue to the work of an editor rather than the author. N. M. Sarna notes concerning the items in chapter 30 that “all the materials for these final items were anticipated in the list of invited donations in 25:3-6” and that they were not needed for installing Aaron and his sons (Exodus [JPSTC], 193). Verses 1-10 can be divided into three sections: the instructions for building the incense altar (1-5), its placement (6), and its proper use (7-10).

The expression is מִזְבֵּחַ מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת (mizbeakh miqtar qetoret), either “an altar, namely an altar of incense,” or “an altar, [for] burning incense.” The second noun is “altar of incense,” although some suggest it is an active noun meaning “burning.” If the former, then it is in apposition to the word for “altar” (which is not in construct). The last noun is “incense” or “sweet smoke.” It either qualifies the “altar of incense” or serves as the object of the active noun. B. Jacob says that in order to designate that this altar be used only for incense, the Torah prepared the second word for this passage alone. It specifies the kind of altar this is (Exodus, 828).
This is an adverbial accusative explaining the material used in building the altar.
See M. Haran, “The Uses of Incense in Ancient Israel Ritual,” VT 10 (1960): 113-15; N. Glueck, “Incense Altars,” Translating and Understanding the Old Testament, 325-29.

verses.zh: 这坛要四方的，长一肘，宽一肘，高二肘；坛的四角要与坛接连一块。
verses.en: Its length is to be 18 inches[NOTE:1] and its width 18 inches; it will be square. Its height is to be 36 inches,[NOTE:2] with its horns of one piece with it.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “a cubit.”
Heb “2 cubits.”
Heb “its horns from it.”

verses.zh: 要用精金把坛的上面与坛的四围，并坛的四角，包裹；又要在坛的四围镶上金牙边。
verses.en: You are to overlay it with pure gold—its top,[NOTE:1] its four walls,[NOTE:2] and its horns—and make a surrounding border of gold for it.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “roof.”
Heb “its walls around.”
Heb “and make for it border gold around.” The verb is a consecutive perfect. See Exod 25:11, where the ark also has such a molding.

verses.zh: 要做两个金环安在牙子边以下，在坛的两旁，两根横撑上，作为穿杠的用处，以便抬坛。
verses.en: You are to make two gold rings for it under its border, on its two flanks; you are to make them on its two sides.[NOTE:1] The rings[NOTE:2] will be places[NOTE:3] for poles to carry it with.
notes: Since it was a small altar, it needed only two rings, one on either side, in order to be carried. The second clause clarifies that the rings should be on the sides, the right and the left, as you approach the altar.
Heb “And it”; this refers to the rings collectively in their placement on the box, and so the word “rings” has been used to clarify the referent for the modern reader.
Heb “for houses.”

verses.zh: 要用皂荚木做杠，用金包裹。
verses.en: You are to make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

verses.zh: 要把坛放在法柜前的幔子外，对着法柜上的施恩座，就是我要与你相会的地方。
verses.en: “You are to put it in front of the curtain that is before the ark of the testimony (before the atonement lid that is over the testimony), where I will meet you.

verses.zh: 亚伦在坛上要烧馨香料做的香；每早晨他收拾灯的时候，要烧这香。
verses.en: Aaron is to burn sweet incense[NOTE:1] on it morning by morning; when he attends to[NOTE:2] the lamps he is to burn incense.[NOTE:3]
notes: The text uses a cognate accusative (“incense”) with the verb “to burn” or “to make into incense/sweet smoke.” Then, the noun “sweet spices” is added in apposition to clarify the incense as sweet.

The Hebrew is בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ (behetivo), a Hiphil infinitive construct serving in a temporal clause. The Hebrew verb means “to make good” and so in this context “to fix” or “to dress.” This refers to cleansing and trimming the lamps.

The point of the little golden altar of incense is normally for intercessory prayer, and then at the Day of Atonement for blood applied atonement. The instructions for making it show that God wanted his people to make a place for prayer. The instructions for its use show that God expects that the requests of his people will be pleasing to him.

verses.zh: 黄昏点灯的时候，他要在耶和华面前烧这香，作为世世代代常烧的香。
verses.en: When Aaron sets up the lamps around sundown he is to burn incense on it; it is to be a regular incense offering before the Lord throughout your generations.

verses.zh: 在这坛上不可奉上异样的香，不可献燔祭、素祭，也不可浇上奠祭。
verses.en: You must not offer strange incense on it, nor burnt offering, nor meal offering, and you must not pour out a drink offering on it.

verses.zh: 亚伦一年一次要在坛的角上行赎罪之礼。他一年一次要用赎罪祭牲的血在坛上行赎罪之礼，作为世世代代的定例。这坛在耶和华面前为至圣。」
verses.en: Aaron is to make atonement on its horns once in the year with some of the blood of the sin offering for atonement;[NOTE:1] once in the year[NOTE:2] he is to make atonement on it throughout your generations. It is most holy to the Lord.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The word “atonements” (plural in Hebrew) is a genitive showing the result or product of the sacrifice made.

This ruling presupposes that the instruction for the Day of Atonement has been given, or at the very least, are to be given shortly. That is the one day of the year that all sin and all ritual impurity would be removed.
The phrase “most holy to the Lord” means that the altar cannot be used for any other purpose than what is stated here.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses,[NOTE:2]
notes: This brief section has been interpreted a number of ways by biblical scholars (for a good survey and discussion, see B. Jacob, Exodus, 829-35). In this context the danger of erecting and caring for a sanctuary may have been in view. A census would be taken to count the losses and to cover the danger of coming into such proximity with the holy place; payment was made to ransom the lives of the people numbered so that they would not die. The money collected would then be used for the care of the sanctuary. The principle was fairly straightforward: Those numbered among the redeemed of the Lord were to support the work of the Lord to maintain their fellowship with the covenant. The passage is fairly easy to outline: I. Every covenant member must give a ransom for his life to avoid death (11-12); II. The ransom is the same for all, whether rich or poor (13-15); and III. The ransom money supports the sanctuary as a memorial for the ransomed (16).

Heb “and Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying.” This full means for introducing a quotation from the Lord is used again in 30:17, 22; 31:1; and 40:1. It appears first in 6:10. Cynthia L. Miller discusses its use in detail (The Representation of Speech in Biblical Hebrew Narrative, 373-86).

verses.zh: 「你要按以色列人被数的，计算总数，你数的时候，他们各人要为自己的生命把赎价奉给耶和华，免得数的时候在他们中间有灾殃。
verses.en: “When you take a census[NOTE:1] of the Israelites according to their number,[NOTE:2] then each man is to pay a ransom[NOTE:3] for his life to the Lord when you number them,[NOTE:4] so that there will be no plague among them when you number them.
notes: The expression is “when you take [lift up] the sum [head] of the Israelites.”

The form is לִפְקֻדֵיהֶם (lifqudehem, “according to those that are numbered of/by them”) from the verb פָּקַד (paqad, “to visit”). But the idea of this word seems more to be that of changing or determining the destiny, and so “appoint” and “number” become clear categories of meaning for the word. Here it simply refers to the census, but when this word is used for a census it often involves mustering an army for a military purpose. Here there is no indication of a war, but it may be laying down the principle that when they should do this, here is the price. B. Jacob (Exodus, 835) uses Num 31 as a good illustration, showing that the warrior was essentially a murderer, if he killed anyone in battle. For this reason his blood was forfeit; if he survived he must pay a כֹּפֶר (kofer) because every human life possesses value and must be atoned for. The payment during the census represented a “presumptive ransom” so that they could not be faulted for what they might do in war.

The “ransom” is כֹּפֶר (kofer), a word related to words translated “atone” and “atonement.” Here the noun refers to what is paid for the life. The idea is that of delivering or redeeming by a substitute—here the substitute is the money. If they paid the amount, their lives would be safe (W. C. Kaiser, Jr., “Exodus,” EBC 2:473).

The temporal clause uses a preposition, an infinitive construct, and then an accusative. The subject is supplied: “in numbering them” means “when [you] number them.” The verb could also be rendered “when you muster them.”

verses.zh: 凡过去归那些被数之人的，每人要按圣所的平，拿银子半舍客勒；这半舍客勒是奉给耶和华的礼物（一舍客勒是二十季拉）。
verses.en: Everyone who crosses over to those who are numbered[NOTE:1] is to pay this: a half shekel[NOTE:2] according to the shekel of the sanctuary[NOTE:3] (a shekel weighs 20 gerahs). The half shekel is to be an offering[NOTE:4] to the Lord.
notes: Each man was to pass in front of the counting officer and join those already counted on the other side.
The half shekel weight of silver would be about one-fifth of an ounce (6 grams).

It appears that some standard is in view for the amount of a shekel weight. The sanctuary shekel is sometimes considered to be twice the value of the ordinary shekel. The “gerah,” also of uncertain meaning, was mentioned as a reference point for the ancient reader to understand the value of the required payment. It may also be that the expression meant “a sacred shekel” and looked at the purpose more—a shekel for sanctuary dues. This would mean that the standard of the shekel weight was set because it was the traditional amount of sacred dues (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 333). “Though there is no certainty, the shekel is said to weigh about 11,5 grams…. Whether an official standard is meant [by ‘sanctuary shekel’] or whether the sanctuary shekel had a different weight than the ‘ordinary’ shekel is not known” (C. Houtman, Exodus, 3:181).
Or “contribution” (תְּרוּמָה, terumah).

verses.zh: 凡过去归那些被数的人，从二十岁以外的，要将这礼物奉给耶和华。
verses.en: Everyone who crosses over to those numbered, from twenty years old and up, is to pay an offering to the Lord.

verses.zh: 他们为赎生命将礼物奉给耶和华，富足的不可多出，贫穷的也不可少出，各人要出半舍客勒。
verses.en: The rich are not to pay more and the poor are not to pay less than the half shekel when giving[NOTE:1] the offering of the Lord, to make atonement[NOTE:2] for your lives.
notes: The form is לָתֵת (latet), the Qal infinitive construct with the lamed preposition. The infinitive here is explaining the preceding verbs. They are not to increase or diminish the amount “in paying the offering.” The construction approximates a temporal clause.
This infinitive construct (לְכַפֵּר, lekhapper) provides the purpose of giving the offering—to atone.

verses.zh: 你要从以色列人收这赎罪银，作为会幕的使用，可以在耶和华面前为以色列人作纪念，赎生命。」
verses.en: You are to receive the atonement money[NOTE:1] from the Israelites and give it for the service[NOTE:2] of the tent of meeting. It will be a memorial[NOTE:3] for the Israelites before the Lord, to make atonement[NOTE:4] for your lives.”
notes: Heb “the silver of the atonements.” The genitive here is the result (as in “sheep of slaughter”) telling what the money will be used for (see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 11, §44).
The idea of “service” is maintenance and care of the sanctuary and its service, meaning the morning and evening sacrifices and the other elements to be used.
S. R. Driver says this is “to keep Jehovah in continual remembrance of the ransom which had been paid for their lives” (Exodus, 334).

The infinitive could be taken in a couple of ways here. It could be an epexegetical infinitive: “making atonement.” Or it could be the infinitive expressing result: “so that atonement will be made for your lives.”

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses,[NOTE:2]
notes: Another piece of furniture is now introduced, the laver, or washing basin. It was a round (the root means to be round) basin for holding water, but it had to be up on a pedestal or base to let water run out (through taps of some kind) for the priests to wash—they could not simply dip dirty hands into the basin. This was for the priests primarily to wash their hands and feet before entering the tent. It stood in the courtyard between the altar and the tent. No dimensions are given. The passage can be divided into three sections: the instructions (17-18), the rules for washing (19-20), and the reminder that this is a perpetual statute.
Heb “and Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying.”

verses.zh: 「你要用铜做洗濯盆和盆座，以便洗濯。要将盆放在会幕和坛的中间，在盆里盛水。
verses.en: “You are also to make a large bronze[NOTE:1] basin with a bronze stand[NOTE:2] for washing. You are to put it between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it,[NOTE:3]
notes: The metal for this object was obtained from the women from their mirrors (see Exod 38:8).
Heb “and its stand bronze.”
The form is the adverb “there” with the directive qamets-he.

verses.zh: 亚伦和他的儿子要在这盆里洗手洗脚。
verses.en: and Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and their feet from it.[NOTE:1]
notes: That is, from water from it.

verses.zh: 他们进会幕，或是就近坛前供职给耶和华献火祭的时候，必用水洗濯，免得死亡。
verses.en: When they enter[NOTE:1] the tent of meeting, they must wash with[NOTE:2] water so that they do not die.[NOTE:3] Also, when they approach[NOTE:4] the altar to minister by burning incense[NOTE:5] as an offering made by fire[NOTE:6] to the Lord,
notes: The form is an infinitive construct with the temporal preposition ב (bet), and a suffixed subjective genitive: “in their going in,” or, whenever they enter.

“Water” is an adverbial accusative of means, and so is translated “with water.” Gesenius classifies this with verbs of “covering with something.” But he prefers to emend the text with a preposition (see GKC 369 §117.y, n. 1).

The verb is a Qal imperfect with a nuance of final imperfect. The purpose/result clause here is indicated only with the conjunction: “and they do not die.” But clearly from the context this is the intended result of their washing—it is in order that they not die.

Here, too, the infinitive is used in a temporal clause construction. The verb נָגַשׁ (nagash) is the common verb used for drawing near to the altar to make offerings—the official duties of the priest.

The text uses two infinitives construct: “to minister to burn incense”; the first is the general term and expresses the purpose of the drawing near, and the second infinitive is epexegetical, explaining the first infinitive.

The translation “as an offering made by fire” is a standard rendering of the one word in the text that appears to refer to “fire.” Milgrom and others contend that it simply means a “gift” (Leviticus 1-16, 161).

verses.zh: 他们洗手洗脚就免得死亡。这要作亚伦和他后裔世世代代永远的定例。」
verses.en: they must wash[NOTE:1] their hands and their feet so that they do not die. And this[NOTE:2] will be a perpetual ordinance for them and for their descendants[NOTE:3] throughout their generations.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and [then] they will wash.”
The verb is “it will be.”
Heb “for his seed.”

The symbolic meaning of washing has been taught throughout the ages. This was a practical matter of cleaning hands and feet, but it was also symbolic of purification before Yahweh. It was an outward sign of inner spiritual cleansing, or forgiveness. Jesus washed the disciples feet (Jn 13) to show this same teaching; he asked the disciples if they knew what he had done (so it was more than washing feet). In this passage the theological points for the outline would be these: I. God provides the means of cleansing; II. Cleansing is a prerequisite for participating in the worship, and III. (Believers) priests must regularly appropriate God’s provision of cleansing.tn Or “for generations to come”; it literally is “to their generations.”

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses,[NOTE:2]
notes: The chapter ends with these two sections. The oil (22-33) is the mark of consecration, and the incense (34-38) is a mark of pleasing service, especially in prayer. So the essence of the message of the chapter is that the servants of God must be set apart by the Spirit for ministry and must be pleasing to God in the ministry.
Heb “and Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying.”

verses.zh: 「你要取上品的香料，就是流质的没药五百舍客勒，香肉桂一半，就是二百五十舍客勒，菖蒲二百五十舍客勒，
verses.en: “Take[NOTE:1] choice spices:[NOTE:2] 12½ pounds[NOTE:3] of free-flowing myrrh,[NOTE:4] half that—about 6¼ pounds—of sweet-smelling cinnamon, 6¼ pounds of sweet-smelling cane,
notes: The construction uses the imperative “take,” but before it is the independent pronoun to add emphasis to it. After the imperative is the ethical dative (lit. “to you”) to stress the task to Moses as a personal responsibility: “and you, take to yourself.”
Heb “spices head.” This must mean the chief spices, or perhaps the top spice, meaning fine spices or choice spices. See Song 4:14; Ezek 27:22.

Or “500 shekels.” Verse 24 specifies that the sanctuary shekel was the unit for weighing the spices. The total of 1500 shekels for the four spices is estimated at between 77 and 100 pounds, or 17 to 22 kilograms, depending on how much a shekel weighed (C. Houtman, Exodus, 3:576).

Myrrh is an aromatic substance that flows from the bark of certain trees in Arabia and Africa and then hardens. “The hardened globules of the gum appear also to have been ground into a powder that would have been easy to store and would have been poured from a container” (J. Durham, Exodus [WBC], 3:406).

verses.zh: 桂皮五百舍客勒，都按着圣所的平，又取橄榄油一欣，
verses.en: and 12½ pounds of cassia, all weighed[NOTE:1] according to the sanctuary shekel, and four quarts[NOTE:2] of olive oil.
notes: The words “all weighed” are added for clarity in English.
Or “a hin.” A hin of oil is estimated at around one gallon (J. Durham, Exodus [WBC], 3:406).

verses.zh: 按做香之法调和做成圣膏油。
verses.en: You are to make this[NOTE:1] into[NOTE:2] a sacred anointing oil, a perfumed compound,[NOTE:3] the work of a perfumer. It will be sacred anointing oil.
notes: Heb “it.”
The word “oil” is an adverbial accusative, indicating the product that results from the verb (R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, §52).

The somewhat rare words rendered “a perfumed compound” are both associated with a verbal root having to do with mixing spices and other ingredients to make fragrant ointments. They are used with the next phrase, “the work of a perfumer,” to describe the finished oil as a special mixture of aromatic spices and one requiring the knowledge and skills of an experienced maker.

verses.zh: 要用这膏油抹会幕和法柜，
verses.en: “With it you are to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony,

verses.zh: 桌子与桌子的一切器具，灯台和灯台的器具，并香坛、
verses.en: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,

verses.zh: 燔祭坛，和坛的一切器具，洗濯盆和盆座。
verses.en: the altar for the burnt offering and all its utensils, and the laver and its base.

verses.zh: 要使这些物成为圣，好成为至圣；凡挨着的都成为圣。
verses.en: So you are to sanctify them,[NOTE:1] and they will be most holy;[NOTE:2] anything that touches them will be holy.[NOTE:3]
notes: The verb is a Piel perfect with vav (ו) consecutive; in this verse it is summarizing or explaining what the anointing has accomplished. This is the effect of the anointing (see Exod 29:36).
This is the superlative genitive again, Heb “holy of holies.”
See Exod 29:37; as before, this could refer to anything or anyone touching the sanctified items.

verses.zh: 要膏亚伦和他的儿子，使他们成为圣，可以给我供祭司的职分。
verses.en: “You are to anoint Aaron and his sons and[NOTE:1] sanctify them so that they may minister as my priests.
notes: The perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive follows the imperfect of instruction; it may be equal to the instruction, but more likely shows the purpose or result of the act.

verses.zh: 你要对以色列人说：『这油，我要世世代代以为圣膏油。
verses.en: And you are to tell the Israelites: ‘This is to be my sacred anointing oil throughout your generations.

verses.zh: 不可倒在别人的身上，也不可按这调和之法做与此相似的。这膏油是圣的，你们也要以为圣。
verses.en: It must not be applied[NOTE:1] to people’s bodies, and you must not make any like it with the same recipe. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
notes: Without an expressed subject, the verb may be treated as a passive. Any common use, as in personal hygiene, would be a complete desecration.

verses.zh: 凡调和与此相似的，或将这膏膏在别人身上的，这人要从民中剪除。』」
verses.en: Whoever makes perfume like it and whoever puts any of it on someone not a priest[NOTE:1] will be cut off[NOTE:2] from his people.’”
notes: Heb “a stranger,” meaning someone not ordained a priest.
The rabbinic interpretation of this is that it is a penalty imposed by heaven, that the life will be cut short and the person could die childless.

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐摩西说：「你要取馨香的香料，就是拿他弗、施喜列、喜利比拿；这馨香的香料和净乳香各样要一般大的分量。
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “Take[NOTE:1] spices, gum resin,[NOTE:2] onycha,[NOTE:3] galbanum,[NOTE:4] and pure frankincense[NOTE:5] of equal amounts[NOTE:6]
notes: The construction is “take to you,” which could be left in that literal sense, but more likely the suffix is an ethical dative, stressing the subject of the imperative.
This is from a word that means “to drip”; the spice is a balsam that drips from a resinous tree.
This may be a plant, or it may be from a species of mollusks; it is mentioned in Ugaritic and Akkadian; it gives a pungent odor when burnt.
This is a gum from plants of the genus Ferula; it has an unpleasant odor, but when mixed with others is pleasant.
The word “spice” is repeated here, suggesting that the first three formed half of the ingredients and this spice the other half—but this is conjecture (U. Cassuto, Exodus, 400).
Heb “of each part there will be an equal part.”

verses.zh: 你要用这些加上盐，按做香之法做成清净圣洁的香。
verses.en: and make it into an incense,[NOTE:1] a perfume,[NOTE:2] the work of a perfumer. It is to be finely ground,[NOTE:3] and pure and sacred.
notes: This is an accusative of result or product.
The word is in apposition to “incense,” further defining the kind of incense that is to be made.

The word מְמֻלָּח (memullakh), a passive participle, is usually taken to mean “salted.” Since there is no meaning like that for the Pual form, the word probably should be taken as “mixed,” as in Rashi and Tg. Onq. Seasoning with salt would work if it were food, but since it is not food, if it means “salted” it would be a symbol of what was sound and whole for the covenant. Some have thought that it would have helped the incense burn quickly with more smoke.

verses.zh: 这香要取点捣得极细，放在会幕内、法柜前，我要在那里与你相会。你们要以这香为至圣。
verses.en: You are to beat some of it very fine and put some of it before the ark of the testimony in the tent of meeting where I will meet with you; it is to be most holy to you.

verses.zh: 你们不可按这调和之法为自己做香；要以这香为圣，归耶和华。
verses.en: And the incense that you are to make, you must not make for yourselves using the same recipe; it is to be most holy to you, belonging to the Lord.

verses.zh: 凡做香和这香一样，为要闻香味的，这人要从民中剪除。」
verses.en: Whoever makes anything like it, to use as perfume,[NOTE:1] will be cut off from his people.”
notes: Or to smell it, to use for the maker’s own pleasure.

commentary:
CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- I have chosen not to do a detailed verse-by-verse exegesis of these chapters. I am theologically wary of trying
to make the tabernacle applicable to the Christian life.

- This is interesting in understanding Israel's worship practices and procedures. The tabernacle was a physical
way to express the transcendence and immanence of God (see Outline V).

- Most of the details of the tabernacle are not meant to convey theological truth. Jesus is the new
tabernacle/temple (cf. John 2:19)! He, not Israel or her sacrificial system (cf. book of Hebrews), is the focus of NT revelation. God
used Israel to reveal Himself but now Jesus is the full and final revelation (i.e., Matt. 5:17-48; 12:3-6).

- I have done a Special Topic on each of the following vocabulary and concept words in alphabetical order.
